The proposed defense-in-depth improvement may be reasonable, but the claimed no-op/accept-all behavior does not exist here.

judged_text: When CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, `req.headers[...] === process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` compares undefined to undefined and passes. On a deployment where APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is truthily set via some other means (or where the env wiring drifts from the constants.ts derivation), the secret check silently becomes a no-op that accepts every request; the current constants.ts guard makes this latent, but the endpoint itself does not fail closed.

On a deployment where APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is truthily set via some other means (or where the env wiring drifts from the constants.ts derivation), the secret check silently becomes a no-op that accepts every request; the current constants.ts guard makes this latent, but the endpoint itself does not fail closed.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check is `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is `undefined` and the header is absent, this comparison will evaluate as `undefined !== undefined` (false) and therefore *not* reject. However, in this diff the handler is preceded by `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) return 403`, and `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined in `packages/lib/constants.ts` as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which makes the route unreachable when the secret is unset. So it’s not a currently-triggerable defect given the diff, but it is a valid, diff-grounded hardening concern (the endpoint itself doesn’t explicitly fail closed on missing envs).
